data.name: Tirthraj
data.gender_notes: Tirthraj is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Sanskrit words 'tirtha' (pilgrimage) and 'raj' (king), Tirthraj signifies a sovereign protector of holy sites. The name Tirthraj carries the meaning “King of Pilgrimage” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Tirthraj usually hope their child will grow to embody king of pilgrimage and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents divine guidance and spiritual guardianship.
data.etymology: Tirthraj belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “King of Pilgrimage.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Tirthraj total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Tirthraj, as a name, holds a significant cultural importance in Hinduism, as it evokes images of spiritual pilgrimage, devotion, and commitment towards reaching enlightenment.
data.spiritual_significance: Tirthraj represents the spiritual journey towards self-realization and the unwavering quest for seeking the divine and sacred truth. It symbolizes the individual's commitment to the spiritual path and being a guardian or protector of spiritual sites and learning. With this name, an individual is signified as a devotee, a seeker of knowledge, and a teacher, all at once.
data.spiritual_symbolism: A pilgrim who has visited numerous sacred places (Tirthas) in search of spiritual growth and inner peace, becoming a beacon of enlightenment for others. A Tirthraj is one who not only attains self-realization but also guides others towards their spiritual journey.

vedic_reference.note: वेदों, उपनिषदों या अन्य प्राचीन शास्त्रों से नहीं है।

historical_references.reference: The great Hindu scholar and philosopher Adi Shankara, who lived around 788 to 820 AD, is known to have visited several sacred sites (Tirthas) in India during his lifetime. One such site is believed to be Tirthamala (Tirumala) in present day Andhra Pradesh, which is famous for the Tirupati Balaji temple. Adi Shankara is said to have visited this site and performed deep spiritual practices, thereby gaining the title 'Tirthraj'.
historical_references.context: Visit to Tirthamala (Tirumala) and spiritual practices

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name 'Tirthraj' can be found in the 13th century Indian epic 'Mahabharata', where the term is used to describe a person who has visited or bathed in all the sacred pilgrimage sites (Tirthas). These pilgrimages are believed to cleanse one's soul and bring spiritual growth. The character Bhima, one of the Pandava brothers, is referred to as Tirthraj after he completes his pilgrimage to all the sacred sites.
historical_references.context: Completion of pilgrimage to all sacred sites

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Tirthraj' holds significant meaning in Hindu culture, representing one who has crossed numerous 'Tirthas' or holy fords on their spiritual journey. In the modern context, this name resonates with individuals seeking self-discovery and embarking on pilgrimage tours. On Instagram, Tirthraj is often used as a hashtag for posts featuring stunning landscapes and religious sites. On Facebook, it's a group name for communities of like-minded individuals sharing spiritual experiences and knowledge. On LinkedIn, it can be found in the profiles of professionals who have undertaken spiritual journeys and wish to reflect this aspect of their identity in their professional persona.

name_in_real_life.story: Krishna Tirthraj from Delhi, India embodies the meaning of Tirthraj - "King of Pilgrimage". Growing up in a Hindu family, they were taught to honor the spiritual significance of their name and live according to dharma.
